title: The reduced Principal is what handlers read; provider tokens never surface on request.auth
asA: operator building a handler behind the mechanism's session-verify middleware
iWant: request.auth to carry only the reduced Principal, never a Keycloak access token, id_token, or refresh token
soThat: no handler code path can accidentally reason about the realm's raw token surface

acceptanceCriteria.description: A verified request in opaque-handle mode exposes only the reduced Principal on `request.auth`.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a session issued from US-11101 (opaque-handle mode) and a project route wired behind the session-verify middleware
acceptanceCriteria.when: the request is dispatched and the resolved `request.auth` object is inspected for keys
acceptanceCriteria.then: the object contains exactly `principalId`, `provider`, `email`, `roles`, `organisationIds`; no `accessToken`, `idToken`, `refreshToken`, or raw-claims field is present; `principalId` is a stable string starting with the realmSlug followed by a colon

acceptanceCriteria.description: A verified request in stateless mode exposes only the reduced Principal on `request.auth`; no server-side session record was created.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a realm record with `sessionMode='stateless'` and `bearerSource='authorization-header'` and a request carrying a valid Keycloak-minted JWT in the Authorization header
acceptanceCriteria.then: the mechanism verifies the token, populates the reduced Principal, and does not create a session-record entry (the session-record store's `put` port is not invoked); `request.auth` carries only the fields listed in AC-11109-1; no `Set-Cookie` is emitted by the mechanism on this response
